stories.title: Humanoid robots take the stage in Guangzhou
stories.summary: A National Day show puts coordinated humanoid performances and public interaction in the spotlight at the Guangdong Science Center.
paragraphs: China Youth Daily reports that a robot performance program premiered in Guangzhou on September 30, with public shows scheduled for October 1–7 at the Guangdong Science Center. Humanoid robots perform group choreography alongside human entertainers, with robot-dog interaction and audience participation also on the program.

The event brings robotics into a public cultural setting. Coordinated stage performances demonstrate a specific application; they do not establish that the robots can work autonomously across unrelated everyday tasks.

image.caption: Visitors meet the robots at the Guangdong Science Center.

stories.title: AgiBot’s A3 gets a native NetEase Cloud Music integration
stories.summary: Voice-controlled music is scheduled to reach the full-size humanoid on October 15. Music-generated movement remains a development goal.
paragraphs: AgiBot says its A3 humanoid now integrates NetEase Cloud Music at the system level, connecting voice requests, music search, account authentication, and playback. The company plans to make voice song requests available from October 15, with account capabilities dependent on delivered software and authorization.

AgiBot reports pilot testing at Chimelong Spaceship park. Generating gestures from music, an AI DJ, and interactive singing are described as future development directions. Public or commercial music playback requires separate licensing; the pilot does not provide blanket commercial authorization.

image.alt: AgiBot A3 and NetEase Cloud Music partnership announcement
image.caption: AgiBot’s announcement of its A3 music-platform integration.

stories.title: More than 300 robots join the everyday life of a theme park
stories.summary: AgiBot and Chimelong put robots to work across performances, visitor guidance, education, retail, and hospitality in Hengqin.
paragraphs: AgiBot’s September 28 announcement describes a September 24 launch at Chimelong Spaceship park in Hengqin. The company says more than 300 robots are regularly deployed across seven application areas, including entertainment, education, visitor guidance, retail, and hotel services.

The announcement also marks the delivery of AgiBot’s 20,000th robot, an A3 Ultra, to Chimelong. The partners launched a joint tourism-and-robotics research institute and announced a 5G-A robotics application with China Mobile.
These are company-reported deployment figures. The announcement does not provide an independent assessment of reliability, operating cost, or how much human supervision each application requires.

image.caption: Robots and human performers at Chimelong Spaceship park.

stories.title: Unitree releases its humanoid base model and fine-tuning code
stories.summary: The Chinese project README records a September 28 release of UnifoLM-WLA-1.0-Base and tools for adapting the model.
paragraphs: Unitree’s Chinese-language project README lists the September 28 release of UnifoLM-WLA-1.0-Base and fine-tuning code. It follows September releases of perception-model weights and code for training action experts.

Unitree describes UnifoLM-WLA-1.0 as a six-billion-parameter humanoid foundation model trained using approximately 2,500 hours of real-robot data, with a single model covering 64 tabletop and whole-body manipulation tasks. These task and training figures are the company’s reported results, rather than independent benchmarks reproduced by SuperRobots.

image.alt: Unitree UnifoLM-WLA project cover showing humanoid manipulation demonstrations
image.caption: Project cover for Unitree’s UnifoLM-WLA model.

stories.title: A wheeled tennis robot meets Wang Qiang on court
stories.summary: LimX Dynamics and Enhance pair a TRON 2 mobile platform with a tennis-training system at the Billie Jean King Cup finals.
paragraphs: LimX Dynamics says the TENNIIX ULTRA MAX tennis-training robot appeared at the Billie Jean King Cup finals in Shenzhen and interacted on court with professional player Wang Qiang. The system combines Enhance’s TENNIIX PRO AI tennis technology with LimX’s TRON 2 wheeled-leg mobile platform.

The company describes ball tracking, changes in position, and adaptive ball delivery during the demonstration. Its proposed applications include clubs and youth coaching. The announcement documents a demonstration, rather than a quantified comparison with human training partners or evidence of broad commercial adoption.

image.alt: Wang Qiang and the TENNIIX tennis robot on opposite sides of the court
image.caption: TENNIIX and Wang Qiang on court in Shenzhen.

stories.title: Unitree’s G1+ adds stronger joints and richer sensing
stories.summary: The upgraded humanoid brings a two-axis neck, stereo and wide-angle vision, touch sensing, and external power support.
paragraphs: Shangguan News, republished by Sina on September 22, reports that Unitree announced the G1+ on September 14. Unitree’s Chinese product page lists a two-degree-of-freedom neck, upgraded motors, stereo and wide-angle cameras, head touch sensing, external power support, and a six-microphone array.

The manufacturer lists the standard model at RMB 95,000 including tax. It states that specifications vary with configuration and usage, and that some demonstrated functions are still under development. The upgrades describe hardware and interaction capabilities, rather than a guarantee of general-purpose autonomy.

image.alt: Unitree G1+ humanoid robot product image
image.caption: The G1+ humanoid in Unitree’s official product imagery.

stories.title: D-Robotics raises $400 million for robot chips and development tools
stories.summary: The Series C round backs Sunrise chips and a software platform spanning data collection, training, simulation, and deployment.
paragraphs: Shenzhen News reports that D-Robotics announced a US$400 million Series C round on September 17, led by Mirae Asset with participation from Meituan and other investors. The company plans to expand its Sunrise chip portfolio and build software covering data collection, model training, simulation, and inference deployment.

The report says cumulative Sunrise chip shipments exceeded eight million. That figure concerns chips across the company’s product portfolio; it is not a count of humanoid robots. The funding supports the infrastructure used by robot developers, rather than a newly announced robot model.
